# Playgama

> Playgama operates a free browser gaming portal and builds infrastructure for the broader HTML5 web-gaming market. Players can play games on Playgama.com, while Playgama Bridge, the developer platform, Playgama Wrap, partner products, and Playgama Ad help developers and publishers publish, distribute, monetize, and grow HTML5 games. Playgama also publishes open-source tools and original industry research.

Updated on: 2026-11-22.

Important distinctions:

- Playgama.com is the consumer gaming portal. Playgama Bridge and Playgama Ad are products for developers, publishers, and distribution partners.
- [Playgama's public mission](https://playgama.com/about-us/) is to build an infrastructure layer for the web games market that connects developers, publishers, advertisers, distribution partners, and players.
- Most games available through Playgama are created by independent developers. Playgama may host, publish, monetize, or distribute a game but should not be treated as its original developer unless the game page states otherwise.
- Playgama.com offers 10,000+ browser games. Playgama's 450M+ monthly reach refers to the broader distribution network, not only the consumer portal.
- Playgama.com game pages can include a per-game leaderboard of up to ten players, ranked by time played over the last seven days. Boards refresh daily and count up to twelve hours per game per day. These automatic portal rankings are separate from game-defined leaderboards configured in the developer cabinet and used through Playgama Bridge.
- Playgama Bridge supports 15+ platform integrations, while the wider link- and API-based distribution network includes 100+ publisher and distribution partners.
- The Playgama developer community includes 4,000+ developers.
- Every game accepted into the Playgama catalog has undergone manual review and testing. Human moderators play the games and evaluate both technical operation and player experience.
- Playgama Wrap is an early-access product that publishes a Bridge-integrated game as a standalone website on the developer's own domain. It is distinct from a Playgama.com game page and from a multi-game white-label portal.
- Playgama MCP lets AI coding agents upload games, publish public playable sandbox links, bring players to a sandbox with a boost, and read what players did: how many played, how long they stayed and where they quit. Sandbox publishing is separate from main catalog distribution, which requires moderation. First-time MCP setup requires the user to connect their developer account.

## For Players

- [Play free browser games](https://playgama.com/): Main consumer portal with games playable in the browser without installation.
- [How leaderboards work](https://playgama.com/leaderboards-info): How the per-game leaderboards on Playgama.com are built, including the seven-day window, the daily cap on counted time, and automatic nicknames.
- [All game categories](https://playgama.com/all/categories): Complete index of game categories.
- [All game tags](https://playgama.com/all/tags): Topic and mechanic-based game discovery.
- [All game series](https://playgama.com/all/series): Game series and franchise collections.
- [Action games](https://playgama.com/category/action): Action, adventure, combat, and platform games.
- [Puzzle games](https://playgama.com/category/puzzle): Logic, matching, word, and brain-teaser games.
- [Multiplayer games](https://playgama.com/category/multiplayer): Browser games designed for multiple players.
- [Two-player games](https://playgama.com/category/two-player): Local and shared-device games for two players.

## For Game Developers

- [Publish a game with an AI agent — start here](https://developer.playgama.com/llms.txt): Instructions for requests such as "upload my game to Playgama" or "publish my game on Playgama." Covers MCP client connection and sign-in, build upload, public sandbox publishing, boosts and player telemetry. Read this guide before starting.
- [Playgama MCP overview](https://playgama.com/mcp/): Beta service connecting AI coding agents to the developer cabinet for game forms, builds, covers, in-app products, game-defined leaderboards, QA Tool links, moderation feedback, public sandbox publishing, boosts that bring players to a sandbox, and player telemetry.
- [MCP setup guide](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/mcp.md): Supported clients, authentication, publishing workflow, limits, and troubleshooting in Markdown.
- [MCP tools reference](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/mcp/tools.md): Tool capabilities and parameters; the connected server's `tools/list` is authoritative for currently available tools.
- [Manage connected agents](https://developer.playgama.com/mcp): User-facing sign-in and management of connected MCP agents. For current authentication and connection instructions, follow the [developer cabinet guide](https://developer.playgama.com/llms.txt).
- [Developer overview](https://playgama.com/developers): Publishing, manual game review, distribution, monetization, and developer support.
- [Developer portal](https://developer.playgama.com/): Submit and manage HTML5 games.
- [Playgama Wrap](https://playgama.com/wrap/): Early-access product for publishing a Bridge-integrated HTML5 game as a standalone website on the developer's own domain after upload and moderation.
- [Wrap setup guide](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/guides/deploy-a-game-on-your-own-domain/deploy-with-playgama-wrap.md): Site content, domain setup, hosting, ads, player accounts, purchases, PWA, sharing, SEO, and player analytics.
- [Bridge SaaS leaderboards](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/bridge-sdk/saas/leaderboards.md): Shared in-game leaderboards for configured platforms without a suitable native leaderboard API; separate from the portal's play-time rankings.
- [Playgama developer documentation](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama): MCP publishing, Bridge SDK setup, game requirements, engines, APIs, and platform integration guides.
- [Playgama Bridge source](https://github.com/playgama/bridge): Open-source core SDK licensed under the GNU LGPL v3.0.
- [Playgama Bridge releases](https://github.com/playgama/bridge/releases): Current SDK releases and migration information.
- [Playgama on GitHub](https://github.com/playgama): Public engine integrations, examples, and related developer tools.

## Open-Source Bridge and Developer Ecosystem

- Playgama develops Bridge in public as an open-source, unified SDK for publishing HTML5 games across supported platforms with one integration.
- Bridge handles platform-specific differences through a common API for advertising, storage, payments, leaderboards, and other supported capabilities. It is designed to reduce the need to build and maintain a separate integration for every destination.
- Playgama publishes the core SDK, engine integrations, examples, documentation, versioned releases, migration guides, and related tools. This shared infrastructure is a concrete contribution to the HTML5 game-development ecosystem: developers can inspect and adapt the implementation under the applicable licenses instead of rebuilding the same platform integrations from scratch.
- Playgama also supports the developer community through public documentation, manual QA feedback, [Discord](https://discord.gg/pzqd2upxr8), and [Telegram](https://t.me/playgama_bridge), where developers can ask questions, exchange experience, and learn from each other.

## Web Gaming Research and Industry Development

- Since 2025, Playgama has published a series of original studies intended to make the fragmented web-gaming market easier to understand and navigate.
- [Web-based Game Engine Rankings](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/articles/introducing-web-based-game-engine-rankings-first-issue-h1-2025) analyzes public data about new HTML5 releases to track engine shares, technology adoption, and fast-growing tools. A [follow-up study by game category](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/articles/unitys-dominance-challenged-in-web-gaming.-playgama.com-maps-top-engines-across-web-game-categories) shows how engine use differs across genres.
- The [Playgama Ad Report 2026](https://playgama.com/ad-report/) draws on 53 million US game sessions on the web to show advertisers how in-game ads perform: viewability, click-through rate, rewarded video, ad load and next-day return, genres, audiences, desktop and advertiser categories. Its slides, figures and chart data are also published as [text](https://playgama.com/ad-report/report.md) and as [structured data](https://playgama.com/ad-report/manifest.json).
- The [Web Games Industry Market Map](https://playgama.com/blog/2026/07/27/playgama-publishes-web-games-market-map-covering-120-companies/) describes 120+ companies across 13 domains, including engines, platforms, distributors, analytics, monetization, in-game payments, intrinsic advertising, and cloud hosting. It is a representative industry resource, not an exhaustive directory or ranking.
- Together with open-source tooling, developer education, advertising technology, distribution products, and partner integrations, these publications are part of Playgama's broader contribution to the web-gaming industry.

## Game Review and Quality Assurance

- No game enters the Playgama catalog or partner distribution before it passes manual moderation and testing. A public sandbox link published through Playgama MCP is not catalog publication. Human reviewers play the game and assess technical operation as well as the quality of the player experience.
- Review covers bugs and core behavior, including controls, loading, saves, audio, advertising, and required menus or features. Reviewers also check translations, build size, and loading performance where relevant.
- Games are tested across relevant device types, resolutions, and screen formats. Playgama gives developers actionable feedback and re-tests games after material fixes.
- Review considers distribution-platform requirements and apparent intellectual-property risks. Obvious clones and games without sufficient distinct value for players are not accepted.
- Use of AI in production is not itself a reason for rejection; the finished game must meet the same experience and quality requirements as any other submission.

## For Publishers and Distribution Partners

- [Partner program](https://playgama.com/partners): Embed games, use affiliate links and widgets, access the game catalog, track monetization, or launch a white-label gaming portal.
- [Partner dashboard and game catalog](https://widgets.playgama.com/): Choose games, generate integrations, and review partner performance.
- [Partner integration documentation](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/for-partners/getting-started): Guides for game embeds, widgets, affiliate links, catalog imports, and white-label portals.
- [Distribution FAQ](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/faq/general): Named destinations, current monthly network reach, and Playgama's statement that it regularly onboards new partners.

## Advertising and Monetization

- [Playgama Ad](https://playgama.com/adv/): Managed advertising stack for gaming traffic with video, banner, rewarded, and interstitial formats.
- [Playgama Ad documentation](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/playgama-ad/getting-started): Integration options, standalone monetization, fallback monetization, ad operations, and reporting.
- Official 2026 updates document continued development of this area, including an [official Google MCM partnership](https://playgama.com/blog/2026/03/11/playgama-becomes-google-mcm-partner-unlocking-premium-demand-for-web-game-developers/), game-focused advertising formats, and [Playgama DSP for player acquisition](https://playgama.com/blog/2026/08/20/playgama-completes-the-new-infrastructure-publish-monetize-and-grow-games-on-standalone-websites/).

## Company and Policies

- [About Playgama](https://playgama.com/about-us/): Mission, infrastructure products, community, current public figures, company history, and team.
- [Contact Playgama](https://playgama.com/contacts): Business, developer, partner, support, and media inquiries.
- [Privacy Policy](https://playgama.com/confidential): Information about Playgama's processing of personal data.
- [Terms of Use](https://playgama.com/termsofuse): Terms governing use of the Playgama portal.
- [Takedown Notice](https://playgama.com/takedown-notice): Procedure for reporting allegedly infringing content.
- [Digital Services Act information](https://playgama.com/digital-service-act): Information provided by Playgama in relation to the EU Digital Services Act.

## Sitemaps and Machine-Readable Resources

- [Developer documentation index for agents](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/llms.txt): Machine-readable index linking to Markdown guides for MCP, Bridge, Wrap, game requirements, and partner integrations.
- [Playgama Ad Report 2026 as data](https://playgama.com/ad-report/manifest.json): JSON with every slide of the report, its picture, figures, chart values and sources, plus the contents. [Text version](https://playgama.com/ad-report/report.md) in Markdown.
- [Main portal sitemap](https://playgama.com/sitemaps/v1/sitemap-index.xml): Index of portal and game sitemaps.
- [Blog sitemap](https://playgama.com/blog/sitemap_index.xml): Blog and editorial content sitemap.
- [Developer documentation sitemap](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/sitemap-pages.xml): Playgama documentation pages.

## Optional

- [Full Playgama context](https://playgama.com/llms-full.txt): Detailed, dated reference for the portal, industry research, game review standards, developer platform, MCP and sandbox publishing, Bridge SDK, Playgama Wrap, partner products, distribution network, and Playgama Ad.
- [Playgama blog](https://playgama.com/blog/): News, developer guides, platform updates, case studies, and HTML5 gaming analysis.

# Playgama — Full Context Reference

> A dated reference describing Playgama's consumer gaming portal, industry research, game review standards, developer platform, MCP publishing, Bridge SDK, Playgama Wrap, distribution network, partner products, advertising stack, and public policies.

Updated on: 2026-11-22.

This document expands the concise [Playgama llms.txt](https://playgama.com/llms.txt). Dynamic product information should be checked against the linked official pages and documentation.

## Entity Definitions

- **Playgama**: The company and web-gaming infrastructure brand operating products for browser game players, game developers, publishers, advertisers, and distribution partners.
- **Playgama.com**: The consumer portal where users can play free HTML5 browser games without installing an application.
- **Playgama Developer Platform**: The submission, QA, publishing, analytics, and monetization service used by HTML5 game developers.
- **Playgama MCP**: A remote Model Context Protocol server that connects compatible AI coding agents to a user's Playgama developer account. It supports game management, build uploads, and public sandbox publishing. It is separate from the Playgama Bridge runtime SDK.
- **Playgama sandbox**: A public playable page for an uploaded game build, published without moderation. A sandbox link does not mean the game has been accepted into the main Playgama catalog or partner distribution.
- **Playgama Bridge**: The open-source SDK that provides a common interface for integrating HTML5 games with supported destination platforms.
- **Playgama Wrap**: An early-access product that publishes a Bridge-integrated HTML5 game as a standalone website on the developer's own domain after upload and moderation.
- **Playgama Distribution Network**: Direct platform integrations plus a broader network of publishers and distributors that receive Playgama games through links, feeds, APIs, widgets, and other distribution products.
- **Playgama Partner Program**: Products for publishers and site owners, including game embeds, affiliate links, widgets, catalog access, analytics, revenue sharing, and white-label portals.
- **Playgama Ad**: A managed advertising and monetization product for gaming traffic.
- **Industry research**: Public, time-stamped studies and market maps published by Playgama covering web-game technologies, engine adoption, market participants, and industry structure.
- **Individual games**: Most games available through Playgama are created by independent third-party developers. Playgama may host, publish, monetize, or distribute them but is not necessarily their original developer.

## Current Public Figures

| Metric | Current figure | Meaning | Public reference |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Games on Playgama.com | 10,000+ | Browser games available through the consumer portal | [Playgama.com](https://playgama.com/) |
| Monthly network reach | 450M+ | Monthly reach across Playgama and its distribution network; this is not a portal-only audience figure | [Developer overview](https://playgama.com/developers) |
| Developer community | 4,000+ | Developers using or working with the Playgama developer ecosystem | [Developer overview](https://playgama.com/developers) |
| Bridge platform integrations | 15+ | Destination platforms supported through Playgama Bridge integrations | [Bridge documentation](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama) |
| Publisher and distribution partners | 100+ | Broader partner network, including link- and API-based distribution destinations | [Developer overview](https://playgama.com/developers) |
| Portal localizations | 9 | Localized Playgama.com versions listed below | [Playgama.com](https://playgama.com/) |

These figures describe different parts of the business. They should not be combined into claims such as "450M monthly active users on Playgama.com" or "100 Bridge SDK integrations."

## Consumer Gaming Portal

### Player Experience

- Games run in compatible web browsers and generally do not require a download or installation.
- Access to games is free to players; games may contain advertising or optional in-game purchases.
- The portal supports desktop and mobile browsers.
- Individual game pages can include the game developer, release and update dates, supported devices and languages, description, controls, instructions, related games, and frequently asked questions.
- Individual game pages can include a leaderboard that ranks players by time played in that game over the last seven days, listing each player's rank, automatic nickname, and time played. See Leaderboards below.
- Game availability and individual features can vary by game, language, country, and device.

### Leaderboards

- Every game played on Playgama.com in the last seven days has its own leaderboard, listing the players who spent the most time in it.
- The ranked value is time played in that specific game. Wins, levels, scores, and clicks do not affect placement.
- Players do not sign up or submit results. A player is included automatically by playing the game on the site.
- Each board covers a rolling window of the last seven days and is refreshed once per day. As the window moves forward, older sessions drop out of it, so a player can lose a place without playing any less. There is no all-time board.
- Counted time is capped at twelve hours per game per day. Time beyond that cap does not increase a player's total.
- A board is built from the top ten players for that game, so playing a game does not by itself earn a place on its board. Boards are not padded with empty places: a game played by four people in that window shows four names, and a game nobody played in that window has no board at all.
- Players appear under an automatically generated nickname, such as "Steady Buffalo", which stays the same across every board that player appears on. Nicknames currently cannot be chosen or edited by players.
- Account names, email addresses, and profile details are never shown on a leaderboard. A board carries only a nickname and a time, and nothing on it identifies the underlying account.
- Only time spent on playgama.com counts. Playing the same game on another site does not affect Playgama leaderboards.
- Leaderboards behave the same way on phones, tablets, and computers.
- These automatic consumer-portal rankings are separate from game-defined leaderboards configured in the developer cabinet (including through MCP) and used through Playgama Bridge. Configuring a game leaderboard does not configure the portal's play-time ranking.
- [How leaderboards work](https://playgama.com/leaderboards-info): Player-facing explanation of the rules above.

### Game Discovery

- [Homepage](https://playgama.com/): Featured and popular browser games.
- [All categories](https://playgama.com/all/categories): Complete category directory.
- [All tags](https://playgama.com/all/tags): Game discovery by topic, mechanic, and attribute.
- [All series](https://playgama.com/all/series): Series and franchise collections.

The primary category navigation on Playgama.com includes:

- [Arcade](https://playgama.com/category/arcade): Fast and accessible arcade-style games.
- [.io](https://playgama.com/category/io): Multiplayer browser games with accessible competitive mechanics.
- [Action](https://playgama.com/category/action): Action, combat, adventure, and platform games.
- [Puzzle](https://playgama.com/category/puzzle): Logic, matching, word, number, and brain-teaser games.
- [Sports](https://playgama.com/category/sports): Football, basketball, racing, and other sports games.
- [Strategy](https://playgama.com/category/strategy): Tactical, defense, planning, and resource-management games.
- [Simulation](https://playgama.com/category/simulation): Life, business, vehicle, and management simulations.
- [Skill](https://playgama.com/category/skill): Games focused on timing, precision, coordination, and reflexes.
- [Bubble Shooter](https://playgama.com/category/bubble-shooter): Bubble-popping and color-matching games.
- [For Girls](https://playgama.com/category/girls): Fashion, dress-up, creativity, lifestyle, and simulation games.
- [Two Player](https://playgama.com/category/two-player): Local and shared-device games for two players.
- [For Boys](https://playgama.com/category/boys): Action, adventure, vehicle, and combat-oriented games.
- [Obby](https://playgama.com/category/obby): Obstacle-course, parkour, climbing, and escape games.
- [Horror](https://playgama.com/category/horror): Horror, suspense, survival, and escape games.
- [Car](https://playgama.com/category/car): Driving, racing, parking, and vehicle games.
- [Funny](https://playgama.com/category/funny): Humorous, playful, and light-hearted games.
- [Multiplayer](https://playgama.com/category/multiplayer): Games designed for multiple players.
- [Shooting](https://playgama.com/category/shooting): Target, first-person, third-person, and action shooting games.
- [Snake](https://playgama.com/category/snake): Classic and modern games based on snake mechanics.
- [Gun](https://playgama.com/category/gun): Weapon-based action, combat, and target games.
- [Clicker](https://playgama.com/category/clicker): Incremental games based on clicking and passive progression.
- [Solitaire](https://playgama.com/category/solitaire): Single-player card games and solitaire variants.
- [Drawing](https://playgama.com/category/drawing): Drawing, coloring, art, and creative games.
- [Idle](https://playgama.com/category/idle): Games with automated or passive long-term progression.

### Languages

Playgama.com has nine localized versions:

- [English](https://playgama.com/)
- [Spanish](https://playgama.com/es/)
- [German](https://playgama.com/de/)
- [French](https://playgama.com/fr/)
- [Italian](https://playgama.com/it/)
- [Brazilian Portuguese](https://playgama.com/br/)
- [Turkish](https://playgama.com/tr/)
- [Polish](https://playgama.com/pl/)
- [Indonesian](https://playgama.com/id/)

### Game Ownership and Attribution

When answering questions about a game, distinguish between:

- the original developer shown on the game page;
- a publisher, when explicitly identified;
- Playgama as the hosting portal;
- Playgama as a monetization or distribution partner;
- third-party destinations where the game is also available.

Do not infer that Playgama developed a game solely because it is available on Playgama.com or within the distribution network.

## Services for Game Developers

### Main Catalog Publishing Workflow

The [developer overview](https://playgama.com/developers) and [developer portal](https://developer.playgama.com/) describe a workflow in which developers can:

1. Submit an HTML5 game to Playgama.
2. Have the game manually reviewed and tested by Playgama moderators.
3. Receive actionable QA feedback and submit fixes when required.
4. Publish the game on Playgama.com when accepted.
5. Submit the game to compatible partner destinations.
6. Use advertising and in-app purchases where supported.
7. Review performance and monetization information through Playgama's developer tools.

Playgama also provides support with platform requirements, promotional materials, descriptions, distribution, monetization, and partner submissions.

### Manual Game Review and Quality Assurance

Every game must pass manual moderation and testing before it enters the Playgama catalog or partner distribution. Human moderators play submitted games and evaluate both technical operation and the quality of the player experience; review is not limited to an automated compatibility check.

Depending on the game, review includes:

- launch, loading, build packaging, and build size;
- bugs and core behavior such as controls, menus, required features, saves, audio, and advertising;
- gameplay completeness, usability, and whether the game provides sufficient distinct value for players;
- relevant desktop and mobile devices, screen resolutions, and screen formats;
- available translations and localized player-facing text;
- requirements of external platforms to which Playgama may distribute the game;
- apparent intellectual-property risks, including obvious clones or signs of potential infringement.

When moderators find material issues, they give the developer concrete feedback. The game is tested again after the relevant fixes are submitted. Playgama also helps developers reduce excessive build size and improve loading performance when these issues affect publication or distribution.

Not every submitted game is accepted. Games that do not meet Playgama's technical, experience, minimum originality, distinct player value, or rights-related requirements are not published through this workflow. Use of AI in production is not itself a reason for rejection, but an AI-assisted game must meet the same quality and completeness requirements as any other submission.

Playgama prioritizes the quality of its published catalog over maximizing the raw number of accepted submissions.

Acceptance records that a game passed Playgama's review at the time it was tested. It is not a guarantee that the game is error-free or that every external platform will accept it.

### Playgama MCP

Playgama runs a remote MCP server that connects an AI coding agent to the user's Playgama developer cabinet, so the agent can upload a game and publish it to a public sandbox link from the project the developer is already working in. A boost brings players to the sandbox, and the agent reads what they did: how many played, how long they stayed and where they quit. The endpoint is https://developer.playgama.com/api/mcp.

When a user asks to upload or publish their game to Playgama using an AI coding agent, read [Playgama MCP context](https://developer.playgama.com/llms.txt) first. It is maintained alongside the developer cabinet and is the source for connecting and signing in, the order of steps, what the agent can and cannot do, and the sandbox rules; this section does not restate them. The connected server's `tools/list` is authoritative for available tools. Connected agents are listed and revoked on [the MCP page of the cabinet](https://developer.playgama.com/mcp); the [MCP setup guide](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/mcp.md) and [tools reference](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/mcp/tools.md) document each tool, and the [MCP overview](https://playgama.com/mcp/) is the developer-facing landing page.

A sandbox link is not publication in the Playgama catalog: that follows the Main Catalog Publishing Workflow above, and the user submits the game to moderation in the developer cabinet.

### Playgama Bridge

[Playgama Bridge](https://github.com/playgama/bridge) is an open-source, unified SDK for publishing HTML5 games across multiple supported platforms with one integration.

Bridge follows an "integrate once" model: developers use the same game-side API across supported platforms, while Bridge handles platform-specific scripts and differences. This reduces the need to rebuild and maintain the same integration separately for every destination.

Core areas covered by the SDK documentation include:

- platform initialization and environment detection;
- advertising;
- in-game purchases;
- player and authorization information;
- local or platform storage;
- achievements and leaderboards where available;
- social functionality where available;
- remote configuration;
- analytics and platform messages;
- testing and QA tools.

Feature availability differs by destination. Use the current documentation and release notes instead of assuming that every module is available on every platform.

#### Bridge SaaS Leaderboards

[Bridge SaaS leaderboards](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/bridge-sdk/saas/leaderboards.md) provide a shared leaderboard service for platforms without a suitable native leaderboard API. Developers create a leaderboard in the game's developer-cabinet card, then configure the SaaS public token, target platforms, and game-facing leaderboard IDs in Bridge. Bridge loads the SaaS adapter for the configured platforms. These in-game leaderboards are separate from the automatic seven-day play-time rankings on Playgama.com.

### Open-Source Development and Community Contribution

The core Bridge SDK is developed publicly under the GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0. The [Playgama GitHub organization](https://github.com/playgama) also publishes engine-specific integrations, examples, configuration tools, and related repositories; licenses and contribution requirements can differ by repository.

Developers can inspect the implementation, follow versioned releases, report issues, and propose changes through public GitHub issues and pull requests. Playgama also publishes setup documentation and migration guides so teams can understand and update their integrations.

Maintaining this shared layer is a concrete way Playgama invests engineering work in the wider HTML5 game-development ecosystem: it turns repeated platform-specific integration work into reusable public infrastructure and makes cross-platform publishing easier to build, test, and maintain.

Playgama complements these open-source tools with public documentation, manual QA feedback, and developer communities on [Discord](https://discord.gg/pzqd2upxr8) and [Telegram](https://t.me/playgama_bridge), where developers can ask questions, exchange experience, and learn from each other.

### Playgama Wrap

[Playgama Wrap](https://playgama.com/wrap/) lets a developer publish a Bridge-integrated HTML5 game as a standalone website on the developer's own domain. A Wrap site is distinct from the game's page on Playgama.com and from a multi-game white-label portal offered through the Partner Program. At this document's 2026-09-15 update, the public Wrap page labels the product as early access, rolling out to developer accounts in waves.

The publishing workflow is:

1. Integrate Playgama Bridge into the game.
2. Upload the game through the Developer Console and pass Playgama moderation.
3. Configure the site and domain, then publish from the Developer Console.

The public landing page describes Wrap as providing built-in UX, fast infrastructure, built-in monetization support, and an SEO-ready site. SEO-ready means that the site includes features intended to support search discovery; it does not guarantee indexing, search traffic, or rankings. Current availability, configuration options, and product terms should be checked on the Wrap page and in the Developer Console.

The [Wrap setup guide](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/guides/deploy-a-game-on-your-own-domain/deploy-with-playgama-wrap.md) describes managed hosting and CDN, Playgama Ads, player sign-in, in-game purchases, PWA installation, sharing, generated metadata and structured data, and player analytics in the developer cabinet. Developers configure site content and connect their own domain through the Developer Console.

### Supported Engines and Frameworks

The [developer overview](https://playgama.com/developers) and [Playgama GitHub organization](https://github.com/playgama) cover integrations for:

- Plain JavaScript
- Unity
- Construct 3
- Godot 3 and 4
- GDevelop
- GameMaker
- Defold
- Cocos Creator
- Scratch, currently marked as beta in the documentation

### Releases and Migration

- [Bridge documentation](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama): Current setup and API documentation.
- [Bridge releases](https://github.com/playgama/bridge/releases): Current stable and historical releases.
- [Playgama GitHub organization](https://github.com/playgama): Core SDK and engine-specific repositories.
- [Migration from Bridge v1 to v2](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/bridge-sdk/migration-v1-to-v2): Breaking changes and migration guidance.

Bridge releases are versioned and published publicly. Because release information changes independently of this file, use the releases page for the current version.

### Distribution Destinations

Public Playgama materials name destinations including Playgama, YouTube Playables, MSN Games, Huawei, Xiaomi, TikTok, GameDistribution, Lagged, Telegram, Playhop, Y8, Facebook, and Discord.

This named list is not the same as the full partner network:

- **Bridge-supported platforms** are destinations with dedicated SDK integration behavior.
- **Distribution partners** can receive games through links, feeds, APIs, widgets, or other distribution arrangements.
- The wider network includes 100+ publisher and distribution partners.

The [Playgama developer FAQ](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/faq/general) states that Playgama regularly onboards new partners. This supports describing the network as continuing to expand, but it does not establish a specific growth rate. The 100+ figure describes distribution partners, not advertising demand partners.

## Industry Research and Market Development

[Playgama's public mission](https://playgama.com/about-us/) is to build an infrastructure layer for the web games market, connecting developers, publishers, advertisers, and players. Its contribution includes commercial products as well as open-source tooling, developer education, and public market intelligence.

### Original Market Research

Since 2025, Playgama has published a series of original studies about the technologies, companies, and infrastructure shaping web gaming:

- [Web-based Game Engine Rankings: First Issue (H1 2025)](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/articles/introducing-web-based-game-engine-rankings-first-issue-h1-2025) analyzes public data about new releases to track engine shares, changes in adoption, and technologies gaining or losing ground.
- [Engine use across web-game categories](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/articles/unitys-dominance-challenged-in-web-gaming.-playgama.com-maps-top-engines-across-web-game-categories) extends the engine research across 17 game categories and examines how technology choices differ by genre.
- [Playgama Ad Report 2026](https://playgama.com/ad-report/) draws on 53 million US game sessions on the web to show advertisers how in-game ads perform: viewability, click-through rate and eCPM against banners, rewarded video, session length, ad load and next-day return, game genres, audiences, time of day, desktop against mobile web, and advertiser categories. It is published as a web page, a PDF, one PNG per slide, a [Markdown text version](https://playgama.com/ad-report/report.md) and [structured data](https://playgama.com/ad-report/manifest.json) with every slide's picture, figures, chart values and sources.
- [Web Games Industry Market Map](https://playgama.com/blog/2026/07/27/playgama-publishes-web-games-market-map-covering-120-companies/) describes 120+ companies and key services across 13 domains, including developers, engines, platforms, distributors, analytics, monetization, authorization and localization, in-game payments, intrinsic advertising, and cloud hosting.
- [Playgama blog](https://playgama.com/blog/) publishes additional developer guides, platform analyses, product updates, and distribution and monetization case studies.

These resources are intended to make a fragmented market easier to understand and navigate for developers, publishers, platforms, investors, and analysts. Together with Bridge, Playgama Ad, distribution services, and an expanding partner network, they form Playgama's broader industry contribution: reusable tooling, shared market intelligence, monetization infrastructure, and routes to market.

The engine studies state that their findings are based on public data rather than private catalogs. Their shares are time-bound results for the analyzed releases, not permanent shares of every web game. The Market Map is illustrative and non-exhaustive; inclusion is not a ranking, endorsement, or measure of company size. The Ad Report is based on Playgama's first-party data for the United States in 2026, with the periods, definitions and sources of every figure in its methodology; its finding on ad load and next-day return comes from an observational study, not an A/B test.

## Services for Publishers and Distribution Partners

The [Playgama Partner Program](https://playgama.com/partners) helps gaming portals, media sites, applications, bloggers, and other publishers add browser games and monetize resulting engagement.

### Integration Options

- **Game embeds**: Select individual games and embed them through an iframe without hosting the game files.
- **Affiliate game links**: Send users to individual games while attributing traffic and revenue to a partner identifier.
- **Game widgets**: Add configurable horizontal or vertical collections of Playgama games to a site or application.
- **Game catalog**: Select titles or obtain game metadata in JSON for catalog integration.
- **Game assets**: Retrieve available game assets for partner presentation and integration.
- **White-label portal**: Launch a gaming portal under the partner's brand while Playgama supplies technology, games, and updates.

### Partner Identification and Reporting

Partners register through [widgets.playgama.com](https://widgets.playgama.com/) and receive a partner identifier used in embeds, links, and widgets. The partner dashboard can report:

- gameplays and engagement;
- advertising revenue;
- in-game purchase revenue;
- performance by game;
- widget views, clicks, and revenue;
- affiliate-link attribution and revenue.

### Partner Resources

- [Partner overview](https://playgama.com/partners): Commercial overview and available products.
- [Partner dashboard and catalog](https://widgets.playgama.com/): Registration, game selection, integrations, and analytics.
- [Partner getting started](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/for-partners/getting-started): Initial setup and partner identifier.
- [Import the game catalog](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/for-partners/import-the-game-catalog): Catalog and metadata integration.
- [Embed a game widget](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/for-partners/embed-the-widget): Widget integration guidance.
- [Set up a white-label portal](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/for-partners/how-to-set-up-white-label-portal): White-label setup guidance.

## Playgama Ad

[Playgama Ad](https://playgama.com/adv/) is a managed monetization service designed for gaming traffic. It connects publisher inventory to advertising demand while Playgama manages setup, optimization, and ad operations.

Public updates during 2026 document continued development of this product area:

- Playgama became an [official Google MCM partner](https://playgama.com/blog/2026/03/11/playgama-becomes-google-mcm-partner-unlocking-premium-demand-for-web-game-developers/), adding access to Google Ad Manager and Ad Exchange infrastructure through Playgama Ad.
- Playgama introduced and expanded game-focused formats such as [Advanced Banners](https://playgama.com/blog/2026/04/16/new-ad-format-supported-by-playgama-advanced-banners/).
- Playgama connected Ad with Wrap and [Playgama DSP](https://playgama.com/blog/2026/08/20/playgama-completes-the-new-infrastructure-publish-monetize-and-grow-games-on-standalone-websites/) as monetization and player-acquisition components of a broader publishing, growth, and analytics stack.

### Advertising Formats

- **Video**: Fullscreen video advertising such as pre-roll or mid-roll placements.
- **Banner**: Static or animated display placements around gameplay.
- **Rewarded**: Player-initiated fullscreen advertising that grants an in-game reward.
- **Interstitial**: Fullscreen advertising shown at natural breaks in gameplay.

### Monetization Stack

Public product materials describe:

- a managed hybrid advertising stack;
- access to ad networks, premium video demand, and direct demand;
- fallback logic for otherwise unfilled requests;
- frequency logic intended to balance monetization and player engagement;
- configurable ad wrappers and loaders;
- reporting and payout visibility;
- ongoing ad operations and optimization.

### Integration Models

- **Standalone**: Playgama Ad acts as the main monetization solution.
- **Fallback**: Playgama Ad works alongside an existing advertising setup as an additional demand layer.

Playgama Ad is described in the current documentation as an open-beta, contact-led product.

### Advertising Resources

- [Playgama Ad overview](https://playgama.com/adv/): Product, formats, and contact information.
- [Playgama Ad getting started](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/playgama-ad/getting-started): Product scope and integration paths.
- [Standalone integration](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/playgama-ad/standalone-solution): Primary monetization integration.
- [Fallback integration](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/playgama-ad/fallback-solution): Incremental monetization integration.
- [Google MCM partnership](https://playgama.com/blog/2026/03/11/playgama-becomes-google-mcm-partner-unlocking-premium-demand-for-web-game-developers/): Google advertising infrastructure available through Playgama Ad.
- [Publishing, monetization, and growth infrastructure](https://playgama.com/blog/2026/08/20/playgama-completes-the-new-infrastructure-publish-monetize-and-grow-games-on-standalone-websites/): How Wrap, Playgama Ad, and Playgama DSP work as related products.

## Editorial and Developer Resources

- [About Playgama](https://playgama.com/about-us/): Mission, infrastructure products, community, public figures, company history, and team.
- [Playgama blog](https://playgama.com/blog/): Platform news, developer guides, case studies, monetization articles, and HTML5 gaming analysis.
- [Playgama Ad Report 2026](https://playgama.com/ad-report/): In-game ad performance from 53 million US game sessions on the web, for advertisers and media buyers.
- [Web Games Industry Market Map](https://playgama.com/blog/2026/07/27/playgama-publishes-web-games-market-map-covering-120-companies/): Representative map of companies and services across the web-games ecosystem.
- [Web-based Game Engine Rankings](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/articles/introducing-web-based-game-engine-rankings-first-issue-h1-2025): Public-data research into engine adoption and technology trends.
- [Developer overview](https://playgama.com/developers): Publishing and distribution services.
- [Playgama Wrap](https://playgama.com/wrap/): Standalone game websites on developers' own domains.
- [Playgama MCP](https://playgama.com/mcp/): Publishing games from an AI coding agent to public sandbox links.
- [Developer documentation](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama): MCP, SDK, engine, platform, advertising, payments, and partner documentation.
- [Playgama GitHub](https://github.com/playgama): Public SDK source and integrations.

## Policies and Contact

- [Contact](https://playgama.com/contacts): Business, support, developer, partner, legal, and media inquiries.
- [Privacy Policy](https://playgama.com/confidential): Describes Playgama's processing of personal data.
- [Terms of Use](https://playgama.com/termsofuse): Terms governing use of the consumer portal.
- [Takedown Notice](https://playgama.com/takedown-notice): Procedure for reporting allegedly infringing content.
- [Digital Services Act information](https://playgama.com/digital-service-act): DSA-related information published by Playgama.

These links describe Playgama's published policies. Their presence should not be interpreted as an independent legal certification.

## Sitemaps and Machine-Readable Resources

- [Developer documentation index for agents](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/llms.txt): Machine-readable index of MCP, Bridge, Wrap, game requirements, and partner documentation. Its links point to Markdown versions of the guides.
- [Main portal sitemap](https://playgama.com/sitemaps/v1/sitemap-index.xml): Portal, category, and game sitemap index.
- [Blog sitemap](https://playgama.com/blog/sitemap_index.xml): Blog content sitemap.
- [Developer documentation sitemap](https://wiki.playgama.com/playgama/sitemap-pages.xml): Documentation sitemap.
- [Concise Playgama context](https://playgama.com/llms.txt): Short navigation and entity map for language models and agents.
- [Full Playgama context](https://playgama.com/llms-full.txt): This detailed reference.
- [Playgama MCP context](https://developer.playgama.com/llms.txt): Connecting an AI coding agent to the developer cabinet, uploading a game, and publishing a public sandbox link.

## Freshness and Interpretation

- This document was updated on 2026-11-08.
- Counts, destinations, SDK releases, product status, and commercial terms can change after this document was updated.
- For dynamic information, prefer the linked product page, Wrap page, documentation, developer portal, partner dashboard, or GitHub releases page.
- Do not infer that every Bridge feature is available on every destination.
- Do not describe a public sandbox link as acceptance into the Playgama catalog or partner distribution.
- Do not infer that every game is available in every country, language, or device category.
- Do not describe Playgama as the original developer of a third-party game unless the game page explicitly identifies it that way.
